title: Boundary Logic with Credit Data: Loan-Default Prediction
text: vignette walks complete three-phase Boundary Logic workflow credit-risk problem: predicting loan default dataset 45,000 loan applications binary loan_status outcome (1 = default, 0 = repaid). closes section places Boundary Logic’s interpretation side side SHAP model. loan dataset exercises features simple iris example : non-linear, tree-based model — XGBoost classifier, wrapped via bl_wrap_model(). Domain filtering — credit-risk question posed sub-population applicants prior default file. Feature pruning driven Phase 2 — global distance--boundary importance used drop weak variables refit leaner model. Business-motivated actionability constraints — variables (interest rate, credit score) move defined directions; others (age) fixed. External-applicant analysis — scoring explaining brand new application training data. workflow follows three phases: Phase 1: Data preparation, model fitting, CVA biplot construction. Phase 2: Global interpretation — distance boundary, per-variable importance, surrogate model, feature pruning. Phase 3: Local interpretation single applicant — local counterfactual, Shapley attribution, sparse counterfactual. Comparison SHAP: global local SHAP XGBoost model, contrasted Boundary Logic output.

code: loan_raw <- read.csv(   system.file("extdata", "loan_data.csv", package = "boundarylogic") )  loan_encoded <- loan_raw  gender_map    <- c(female = 0, male = 1) ownership_map <- c("MORTGAGE" = 0, "OTHER" = 1, "OWN" = 2, "RENT" = 3) intent_map    <- c("DEBTCONSOLIDATION" = 0, "EDUCATION" = 1,                    "HOMEIMPROVEMENT" = 2, "MEDICAL" = 3,                    "PERSONAL" = 4, "VENTURE" = 5) education_map <- c("High School" = 0, "Associate" = 1,                    "Bachelor" = 2, "Master" = 3, "Doctorate" = 4) defaults_map  <- c("No" = 0, "Yes" = 1)  loan_encoded$person_gender                  <- gender_map[loan_encoded$person_gender] loan_encoded$person_education               <- education_map[loan_encoded$person_education] loan_encoded$person_home_ownership          <- ownership_map[loan_encoded$person_home_ownership] loan_encoded$loan_intent                    <- intent_map[loan_encoded$loan_intent] loan_encoded$previous_loan_defaults_on_file <- defaults_map[loan_encoded$previous_loan_defaults_on_file]  # Coerce all columns to double so the training data and the prediction grid # share the same type (read.csv() reads integer-valued columns as integer, # but the grid builder generates sequences as double). loan_encoded[] <- lapply(loan_encoded, as.numeric)  # Drop high-cardinality categoricals vars_to_remove <- c("loan_intent", "person_education", "person_home_ownership") loan_encoded   <- loan_encoded[, setdiff(names(loan_encoded), vars_to_remove),                                drop = FALSE]  names(loan_encoded) #>  [1] "person_age"                     "person_gender"                  #>  [3] "person_income"                  "person_emp_exp"                 #>  [5] "loan_amnt"                      "loan_int_rate"                  #>  [7] "loan_percent_income"            "cb_person_cred_hist_length"     #>  [9] "credit_score"                   "previous_loan_defaults_on_file" #> [11] "loan_status"

text: every variable can move freely lending decision. set_filters() encodes business constraints: "decrease" — counterfactual value must ≤ observed. "increase" — counterfactual value must ≥ observed. "fixed" — actionable; search allows ±0.5 observed, restores observed value. restored point longer crosses boundary, leaves training ranges, counterfactual reported, reported counterfactual always holds feature exactly. c(min, max) — counterfactual must lie within absolute range. "integer" — whole number raw units (count score), alone combined: c("increase", "integer") list(c(min, max), "integer"). counterfactual rounded search re-checked; without feature continuous. person_age fixed (actionable), loan_int_rate credit_score constrained increase. variables still reduced model may named.

text: boundarylogic R package operationalises PhD methodology post-hoc interpretability binary classification models. projects high-dimensional data 2D biplot (PCA CVA), approximates model’s decision boundary space, finds counterfactuals — minimum change observation flips prediction. Three-phase workflow: - Phase 1: data prep → model → biplot projection → prediction grid → bl_result (central anchor object) - Phase 2 (global): nearest boundary point per observation, surrogate model, robustness - Phase 3 (local): single-observation biplot rotation → counterfactual → Shapley attribution → sparse counterfactual bl_result object everything downstream consumes.

title: Biplot-Based Decision Boundary Interpretability for Classification Models
code: library(boundarylogic)  # Phase 1: prepare data, fit model, build biplot bl_dat <- bl_prepare_data(   data           = iris,   class_col      = "Species",   target_class   = "versicolor",   # 1 = versicolor, 0 = all others   train_fraction = 0.8,   seed           = 42L,   hull_fraction  = 0.9             # drop the outermost 10% of training points )  bl_mod <- bl_fit_model(   train_data = bl_dat$train_data,   var_names  = bl_dat$var_names,   model_type = "GLM" )  bl_results <- bl_build_result(   bl_data  = bl_dat,   bl_model = bl_mod,   method   = "PCA",   b_margin = 0.001                 # contour band: cutoff +/- 0.001 (the default) )  plot_biplotEZ(bl_results)  # Overlay test data test_pts <- bl_project_points(bl_results$test_data, bl_results) plot_biplotEZ(bl_results, points = test_pts) # Phase 2: global counterfactual search bl_bnd <- bl_find_boundary(bl_results) plot(bl_bnd)                   # jitter plot — per-variable distances + robustness plot(bl_bnd, type = "boxplot") # boxplot by confusion category  bl_sur <- bl_surrogate(bl_results) plot(bl_sur) # Phase 3: local interpretation of one observation pred_summary <- bl_predict(bl_results) tdp <- which(pred_summary$pred_class == 1)[1]   # first predicted class-1 row tgt <- bl_select_target(bl_results, target = tdp)  bl_local <- bl_find_local_cf(bl_results, tgt) plot(bl_local)  bl_shapley_values <- bl_shapley(bl_local) plot(bl_shapley_values)  bl_sparse <- bl_find_sparse_cf(bl_shapley_values) print(bl_sparse) plot(bl_sparse)

code: # Example: custom GAM with spline terms (Pima diabetes dataset, bundled) library(mgcv)  pima_raw <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "pima_diabetes.csv",                                  package = "boundarylogic")) # Zeros in these columns are missing values; keep complete rows only pima <- pima_raw[with(pima_raw, Glucose != 0 & BloodPressure != 0 &                         SkinThickness != 0 & Insulin != 0 & BMI != 0), ]  bl_dat_pima <- bl_prepare_data(   data          = pima,   class_col     = "Outcome",       # already 0/1   feature_cols  = c("Pregnancies", "Glucose", "BloodPressure",                     "Insulin", "BMI", "Age"),   hull_fraction = 1                # no outlier trimming )  custom_gam <- mgcv::gam(   class ~ s(Glucose) + s(BMI) + s(BloodPressure) + Insulin + Age + Pregnancies,   data   = bl_dat_pima$train_data,   family = binomial(link = "logit") )  bl_mod_pima <- bl_wrap_model(   model      = custom_gam,   model_type = "custom",           # or model_type = "GAM", with no predict_fn   var_names  = bl_dat_pima$var_names,   predict_fn = function(m, new_data) {     as.numeric(mgcv::predict.gam(m, newdata = new_data, type = "response"))   },   train_data = bl_dat_pima$train_data )  bl_results_pima <- bl_build_result(bl_dat_pima, bl_mod_pima,                                    method = "CVA", b_margin = 0.01) plot_biplotEZ(bl_results_pima)

text: Phase 1 — data preparation (bl_prepare_data(), bl_wrap_data(), bl_filter_outliers()), model fitting/wrapping (bl_fit_model(), bl_wrap_model()), PCA/CVA biplot projection (bl_build_projection()), prediction-grid decision-boundary contour construction (bl_build_grid()), assembly central bl_result anchor object (bl_assemble(), bl_build_result()), plot_biplotEZ() visualisation.
